title: For Ever Here My Rest Shall Be
description: For Ever Here My Rest Shall Be in Tonic Solfa to YORK, doh is F: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: John Wesley printed these words in A Collection of Hymns for the Use of the People Called Methodists (1780), hymn 346. They first appeared in a book he and his brother Charles published together, and the Collection's own index cannot say which of the two wrote them.
The book printed the words without tunes. They are in Common Metre (8.6.8.6), and this page sets them to YORK; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: For ev-er here my rest shall be, Close to thy bleed-ing side; This all my hope, and all my plea, For me the Sa-viour died!

lines: For ever here my rest shall be,
This all my hope, and all my plea,
My dying Saviour, and my God,
Sprinkle me ever with thy blood,
And cleanse, and keep me clean.
Wash me, and make me thus thine own,
Wash me, and mine thou art,
Wash me, but not my feet alone,
My hands, my head, my heart.
The atonement of thy blood apply,
Till hope in full fruition die,
And all my soul be love.

source: John Wesley, A Collection of Hymns for the Use of the People Called Methodists (1780)
licence: Public domain: Charles Wesley died in 1788; John Wesley died in 1791.
credits: Words by Charles Wesley (1707–1788) or John Wesley (1703–1791), public domain, as printed in John Wesley's Collection of Hymns (1780); set to YORK by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
